## Goal

Any npm package works on demand, offline works for everything in the store, one React copy, and install scripts never run with the supervisor's authority.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | The curated warm set resolves instantly for every artifact with one React copy | I | Warm-set imports resolve without install; runtime check shows one React instance with an on-demand peer-dependent package |
| DP-02 | Any npm package installs on demand into a shared content-addressed store with a per-artifact lockfile; a host policy `dependencies: "explicit"` turns unknown imports into `MOSTRA_DEP_MISSING` with the exact `mostra add` command | I, X | Unknown import installs into the shared store with a per-artifact lockfile; explicit policy returns MOSTRA_DEP_MISSING with the command; external: real npm |
| DP-03 | The lockfile hash is part of version identity; a frozen version rebuilds offline from the store | I | Lockfile change changes envDigest; frozen version rebuilds offline from the store |
| DP-04 | A missing package offline produces a structured error, never a hang | I | Offline missing package returns MOSTRA_DEP_OFFLINE within 1 s (timer assertion), no hang |
| DP-05 | Package lifecycle scripts run in the artifact's execution context, not the supervisor's | I | Lifecycle script records its PID, cwd and environment; they belong to the install child in the artifact context |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

the warm-set resolver with one React copy; on-demand installs into the shared store with per-artifact lockfiles, run in an install child in the artifact's context; the lockfile digest in `envDigest`; offline mode; the `explicit` policy and `MOSTRA_DEP_MISSING`; `mostra add`.

Design detail for this package:

- Use pnpm's MIT store and linking through its programmatic or CLI interface, never `pnpr/`; installs run in an install child with the artifact's cwd and environment.
- The warm set is a pre-built layout inside the runtime; resolution prefers it; on-demand packages declare warm packages as peers so React stays single.
- `mostra add`, the `explicit` policy, `MOSTRA_DEP_MISSING`, `MOSTRA_DEP_OFFLINE`, `MOSTRA_DEP_TIMEOUT`.

- Kit-specific packs (WP-18)

## Acceptance evidence

- one React instance at runtime with an on-demand package that peer-depends on React;
- an offline rebuild of a frozen version from the store;
- an offline missing package returns a structured error within 1 s;
- a lifecycle script runs with the artifact's cwd and environment, not the supervisor's (observed through its PID and environment);
- an external npm install, labelled as external evidence.

Also: `pnpm check` green (from WP-01 on), diff reviewed, evidence matrix rows updated, docs and AGENTS.md current, progress report written after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- Peer resolution across store layouts can duplicate React: the single-instance check is a test, not an assumption.

## Handoff

A lockfile per version and a store any later package installs into.
